groups.name: stx.migrations
groups.description: Schema migrations run before the context finishes refreshing.

properties.name: stx.migrations.enabled
properties.description: Run the migrations before the context finishes refreshing, and refuse to start if any of them fails. Off by default.

properties.name: stx.migrations.store
properties.description: Which ledger to build: mongo over the MongoDatabase bean, or sql over the Jpa bean. Unset means build none, because the application declares its own MigrationRunner bean. Nothing is inferred: an application with both beans is not saying which schema it means to migrate. An application migrating both names one here and declares a runner for the other.

properties.name: stx.migrations.name
properties.description: The table or collection the ledger lives in. The lock lives beside it, in <name>_lock. Worth changing only when something else already owns that name.

properties.name: stx.migrations.lease
properties.description: How long the migration lock is good for before the process holding it is assumed gone. Default 5m. Not a deadline on a migration: the lock renews at a third of this while the work runs.

properties.name: stx.migrations.lock-timeout
properties.description: How long to wait for another instance to finish migrating before giving up and failing to start. Default 5m. Generous on purpose: an instance that gave up and started serving would serve against a schema that does not exist yet.

properties.name: stx.migrations.lock-poll
properties.description: How long to wait between two attempts on the migration lock. Default 1s.

properties.name: stx.migrations.stale-after
properties.description: How old a RUNNING record has to be before it is read as a process that died rather than one that is slow. Default 15m. Only consulted while this instance holds the lock, so a live holder is never mistaken for a dead one.

values.description: Over the MongoDatabase bean — stx.mongo's, or the one stx.data.mongo bridges from Spring Data.
Over the Jpa bean stx.jpa opened. PostgreSQL and MySQL; DB2 is refused by name.
